RAJYA SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday, November 23, 2010/Agrahayana 2, 1932 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Civil Aviation; Finance; Health and Family Welfare; Heavy
Industries and Public Enterprises; Panchayati Raj; Petroleum and
Natural Gas; Rural Development; Shipping)
Total number of questions — 20
Acute shortage of LPG in
Tamil Nadu
*181. SHRIMATI V ASANTHI
STANLEY: W ill the Minister of
PETROLEUM AND NA TURAL GAS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is an
acute shortage of LPG for domestic use as
compared to the demand in Tamil Nadu;
(b) if so, the reasons for this shortage
prevailing in the State, presently;
(c) whether it is also a fact that it takes
more than ten to fifteen days to get a refill
for LPG at various places across the State;
(d) the steps being taken to ease the
supply vis-á-vis the demand prevailing in
the State; and
(e) by when the situation is likely to
improve to ensure smooth supply at regular
intervals for the consumers in the State?
 Healthcare system in the country
*182. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA: W ill the Minister of
HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether according to an international
survey, India's healthcare system fails
miserably on almost all parameters in
comparison to many developed or
developing nations;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government is aware that
the healthcare system in rural areas of
the country is pathetic and needs
improvement; and
(d) if so, the steps Government
proposes to take to develop the overall
healthcare infrastructure in the country?
 Medical facilities for treatment of
chronic diseases
*183. SHRI BHAGAT SINGH
KOSHYARI: W ill the Minister of
HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether cases of chronic diseases
like cardiac problem, diabetes, renal failure,
cancer etc. are on the rise in the country,
including rural areas, over the years;

57
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether any study has been
conducted to find out the reasons for it;
(d) if so, the details thereof along with
the funds allocated by Government in this
regard; and
(e) the steps taken by Government to
control such diseases and provide medical
treatment to the patients at low cost,
particularly in the rural areas?
 Diversion of funds meant for
Panchayati Raj Schemes
*184. SHRI NARENDRA KUMAR
KASHYAP: W ill the Minister of
PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to state:
(a) whether the funds meant for
Panchayati Raj Schemes are being spent
after converting the small schemes into big
schemes;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether the funds meant for
backward regions have not been spent;
(d) if so, the reasons therefor;
(e) whether any target has been fixed
for utilising the funds in the districts under
the schemes;
(f) if so, the details thereof; and
(g) the measures taken by Government
to ensure proper utilisation of funds
allocated under Panchayati Raj Schemes?
Subsidy for oil companies
*185. SHRI P. RAJEEVE: W ill the
Minister of  PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has decided
to give more subsidy to petroleum
companies;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) whether the Ministry has decided
to disinvest the public sector oil
companies?
 Reduction in incentives given to
ASHAs
*186. SHRI TARINI KANTA ROY:
Will the Minister of  HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELF ARE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether a fixed monthly
remuneration is being given to the
Accredited Social Health Activists
(ASHAs);
(b) if so, the details thereof, State-wise
during the last three  years;
(c) whether the incentives being given
to ASHAs under the Janani Suraksha Yojana
(JSY) have been reduced;
(d) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(e) the States where incentives being
given to ASHAs under JSY have been
reduced?
 Minimum wages for workers in the
oil sector
*187. SHRI PRAVEEN
RASHTRAPAL: W ill the Minister of
PETROLEUM AND NA TURAL GAS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Ministry has submitted
any proposal to the Ministry of Labour
and Employment for fixing minimum wages
in the oil sector;
(b) if not, the reasons therefor; and
(c) the details regarding wages paid to
regular workers, contingency paid workers,
and contractual workers belonging to all

58
the cadres alongwith term based officers,
as on 1 January, 2010 and contractual
workers in various cadres of assets in
Gujarat?
 High mortality due to malaria in the
country
*188. SHRI S. THANGA VELU: Will
the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the mortality
rate due to malaria in the country is higher
than the actual data  projected by the World
Health Organisation (WHO);
(b) whether it is also a fact that 90 per
cent of deaths due to malaria are in rural
areas, out of which 86 per cent occur at
home without any medical attention;
(c) if so, the details thereof and whether
Government has initiated any specific
programme to control malaria and bring
awareness about this dangerous disease in
rural areas; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and follow-
up action taken by Government in this
regard?
Uniform taxation in all States
†*189. SHRI ANIL MADHA V DAVE:
Will the Minister of  FINANCE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether any matter is under
consideration of Government to bring
uniformity in taxes in all States of the
country; and
(b) if so, the details thereof and by when
a decision in the matter is likely to be
taken?
Change in computation of price index
in the country
†*190. SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD: Will the Minister of FINANCE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
has brought about a substantial change in
the old system of computation of price
index in the country;
(b) if so, whether the number of items
has been increased in the new system;
(c) if so, the total number of items in
the old and new systems respectively;
(d) whether base year has also been
changed for computation; and
(e) if so, the base year at present?
Decontrolling the pricing of diesel
†*191. SHRI UPENDRA
KUSHWAHA: W ill the Minister of
PETROLEUM AND NA TURAL GAS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
has decontrolled the pricing of petrol on
25 June and now a proposal to decontrol
the pricing of diesel is also pending before
Government;
(b) whether with the removal of
Government control on the pricing of diesel,
its price will instantly increase by ` 3 per
litre;
(c) whether the rise in price of diesel
will add to the problems of the farmers
who are already in a bad state and increase
inflation too; and
(d) if so, whether it would be
appropriate to decontrol the price of diesel
keeping in view the farmers and common
people of the country?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

59
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Annual health survey in
Maharashtra
†*192. SHRI ISHWARLAL
SHANKARLAL JAIN: Will the Minister
of  HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE
be pleased to state:
(a) the district-wise details of
Maharashtra where annual health survey
has been conducted under the Annual
Health Survey Scheme;
(b) the details of the outcome of the
said survey and the shortcomings found in
the survey;
(c) whether funds have been allocated
to Maharashtra for the said Scheme; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Immunization of ‘under five’ children
*193. SHRI N. K. SINGH: Will the
Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) the percentage of fully immunized
‘under five’ children in the country as of
now;
(b) the steps taken in the last three years
to achieve the goal of full immunization;
and
(c) the States which have lower
immunization rates than the national
average?
 Hazardous substances lying with
customs at ports
*194. PROF. SAIF-UD-DIN SOZ: Will
the Minister of  FINANCE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that many
hazardous substances have been heaped at
various ports on the Eastern Coast by the
Customs Department;
(b) if so, whether these substances,
which are a health hazard, have not been
removed so far; and
(c) if so, the reasons therefor?
 Impact of GST on textile industry
*195. SHRI GOVINDRAO ADIK: Will
the Minister of  FINANCE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether a section of textile industry
has protested the imminent introduction
of the Goods and Service Tax (GST) on
textile industry;
(b) what will be the tax burden on the
industry under GST  vis-á-vis the present
situation; and
(c) whether the extension of GST to
textile sector is likely to lead to
fragmentation of the textile industry?
 Revision of MGNREGS wages
*196. SHRI T.K. RANGARAJAN:
Will the Minister of RURAL
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether there are demands from
States for the revision of wages under the
Mahatma Gandhi National Rural
Employment Guarantee Scheme
(MGNREGS);
(b) if so, whether Government is
considering to increase the wages in view
of the increased Consumer Price Index
(CPI);
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?

60
 Implementation of Basel II and III
recommendations
*197. SHRIMATI T. RA TNA BAI:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
is implementing Basel II and Basel III
recommendations; and
(b) if so, the details thereof and its
implementation status?
Children living with acute
malnutrition
*198. SHRI D. RAJA: Will the Minister
of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Ministry has taken any
measures to treat eight million children
living with severe acute malnutrition; and
(b) whether the Ministry has drafted a
protocol to treat severe acute malnutrition
in children under five?
 Development of airports in NER for
better air connectivity
*199. SHRI BIRENDRA PRASAD
BAISHYA: Will the Minister of CIVIL
A VIA TION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government proposes to
develop the Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi
International Airport Terminal at Guwahati,
including other airport terminals in North
Eastern States, for better air connectivity
in the region;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government proposes to
open new airports/airfields in the region;
and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Referral of cases of fraudulent firms
to CBI or Interpol
*200. SHRIMA TI KUSUM RAI: Will
the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to
refer to answer to Unstarred Question 2460
given in the Rajya Sabha on 17 August,
2010 and state:
(a) the details of the amount recovered
till date, after acceptance of compromise
proposal by borrowers to pay the huge
outstanding loan amount;
(b) if not, the reasons therefor;
(c) the reasons for not contacting CBI
or Interpol by the Government to initiate
action against the fraudulent firms, which
are responsible for defalcation of such huge
amount of public money;
(d) whether Government will refer the
case to CBI and Interpol to bring fraudulent
firms to justice;
(e) if so, the details thereof; and
(f) if not, reasons for safeguarding the
interest of fraudsters?
N
EW DELHI; V . K. AGNIHOTRI,
The 16th November, 2010 Secretary-General.
Kartika 25, 1932 (Saka)
GMGIPMRND—5188RS(S-3)—13.11.2010.

I N D E X
(Ministry-wise)

Finance : 189, 190, 194, 195, 197, 200,

Panchayati Raj : 184,
Petroleum and Natural Gas : 181, 185, 187, 191,
Rural Development : 196.
